questions.question: $\lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \operatorname{cosec} x\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}-\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)$ is:
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { } \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \operatorname{cosec}\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}-\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right) \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\cos \operatorname{ec} x\left(\cos ^2 x+3 \cos x-\sin x-4\right)}{\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}+\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{1}{\sin x} \frac{\left(\cos ^2 x+3 \cos x-4\right)-\sin x}{\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}+\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\left(\cos ^x+4\right)(\cos x-1)-\sin x}{\sin x\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}+\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{-2 \sin ^2 \frac{x}{2}(\cos x+4)-2 \sin \frac{x}{2} \cos \frac{x}{2}}{2 \sin \frac{x}{2} \cos \frac{x}{2}\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}+\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{-\left(\sin ^x(\cos x+4)+\cos \frac{x}{2}\right)}{\cos \frac{x}{2}\left(\sqrt{2 \cos ^2 x+3 \cos x}+\sqrt{\cos ^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)} \\ & -\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}$

questions.question: If $a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{x4}$ and $b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{sin}^{2}x}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{1 + cosx}}$, then the value of $a{b}^{3}$ is :
questions.solution:
Given: $a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{x4}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}}} - \sqrt{2}}{x4} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} - 2}{{x}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}}} + \sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} - 1}{{x}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{1 + 0}} + \sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ a = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} - 1}{{x}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + 1} + \sqrt{2}\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} - 1}{x4}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} - 1}{x4} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} + 1}{\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} + 1}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 + {x}^{4} - 1}{{x}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + {x}^{4}} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x4}{{x}^{4}\left(\sqrt{1 + 0} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x4}{{x}^{4}\left(2\right)}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x4}{x4}$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}}$

Also, $b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{sin}^{2}x}{\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{1 + cosx}}$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - {cos}^{2}x\right) ( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + cosx} )}{2 - ( 1 + cosx )}$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0}\left(1 - cosx\right)\left(1 + cosx\right) ( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + cosx} )\left(1 - cosx\right)$

$⇒ b = \lim_{x \to 0} ( 1 + cosx ) ( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + cosx} )$

$⇒ b = ( 1 + cos0 ) ( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + cos0} )$

$⇒ b = ( 1 + 1 ) ( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{1 + 1} )$

$⇒ b = ( 2 ) ( 2\sqrt{2} )$

$⇒ b = 4\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ a{b}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}} \times ( 4\sqrt{2}{)}^{3}$

$⇒ a{b}^{3} = 32$

questions.question:
The value of

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1 + 2 - 3 + 4 + 5 - 6 + \ldots + ( 3n - 2 ) + ( 3n - 1 ) - 3n}{\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3}-\sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}}$ is
questions.solution:
The given limit $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{1 + 2 - 3 + 4 + 5 - 6 + \ldots + ( 3n - 2 ) + ( 3n - 1 ) - 3n}{\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3}-\sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}}$ can be expressed as,$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}\left(3r - 2\right) + \left(3r - 1\right) - 3r}{\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{n}3\left(r - 1\right)}{\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{0 + 3 + 6 + 9 + \ldots . nterms}{\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}} . . . . . . . ( 1 )$

We know the sum of the nth term of A.P. is given by

${S}_{n} = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a + \left(n - 1\right)d\right]$

Using above formula in equation(1) we get,

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{3n ( n - 1 )}{2}\left(\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}\right)$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{3n ( n - 1 )}{2\left(\sqrt{2{n}^{4} + 4n + 3} - \sqrt{{n}^{4} + 5n + 4}\right)}$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{3 ( 1 - \dfrac{1}{n} )}{2\left(\sqrt{2 + \dfrac{4}{n3} + \dfrac{3}{n4}} - \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{5}{n3} + \dfrac{4}{n4}}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{3 ( 1 - 0 )}{2\left(\sqrt{2 + 0 + 0} - \sqrt{1 + 0 + 0}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{3}{2 ( \sqrt{2} - 1 )} = \dfrac{3}{2} ( \sqrt{2} + 1 )$

questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\left(\dfrac{1 - {cos}^{2} ( 3x )}{{cos}^{3} ( 4x )}\right)\left(\dfrac{{sin}^{3} ( 4x )}{\left({log}_{e}\left(2x + 1\right)\right)5}\right)\right)$

Now we now that,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx}{x} = 1, \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{1 - cosx}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ and } \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{log\left(1 + x\right)}{x} = 1$

Now using the above formula we get,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\left(\dfrac{1 - {cos}^{2}3x}{{cos}^{3}4x}\right)\left(\dfrac{{sin}^{3}4x}{\left({log}_{e}\left(2x + 1\right)\right)5}\right)\right)$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\left(1 - cos3x\right)\left(1 + cos3x\right)9{x}^{2}}{\left({cos}^{3}4x\right)9{x}^{2}}\dfrac{\left(sin4x\right)3\left(64x\right)3\left(2x\right)5}{\left(64{x}^{3}\right)\left({log}_{e} ( 2x + 1 )\right)5\left(2x\right)5}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1 - cos3x}{9{x}^{2}}\right)\left(1 + cos3x\right)\left({cos}^{3}4x\right)\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{sin4x}{4x}\right)3}{\left(\dfrac{{log}_{e} ( 2x + 1 )}{2x}\right)5} \times \dfrac{9 \times 64}{32}$

$= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(2\right)\left(1\right)\dfrac{\left(1\right)3}{\left(1\right)5} \times \dfrac{9 \times 64}{32}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times 2}{1} = 18$

questions.solution:
Since, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $a{x}^{2} + bx + 1 = 0$, therefore $\dfrac{1}{α}$ and $\dfrac{1}{β}$ would be the roots of ${x}^{2} + bx + a = 0$.

Let

$L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{1 - cos\left({x}^{2} + bx + a\right)}{2\left(1 - \alphax\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2} \to \dfrac{0}{0}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{2{sin}^{2}\left(\dfrac{{x}^{2} + bx + a}{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - \alphax\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{{sin}^{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)\right)}{{α}^{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{1}{α}}\left[\dfrac{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)2}{4{α}^{2}} \times \dfrac{\left\{sin\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)\right)\right\}2}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)2\left(x - \dfrac{1}{α}\right)2\left(x - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ L = \left(\dfrac{1}{α} - \dfrac{1}{β}\right)2\alpha$

On comparing this value with the value given in the question we get, $k = 2\alpha$.

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.solution:
If, $\beta = \lim_{x \to 0}\left(cosx\right)cotx$ (${1}^{\infty}$form)

$\beta = {e}^{\lim_{x \to 0}cotx\left[cosx - 1\right]}$

$\beta = {e}^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- cosx}{sinx}\left[1 - 1 + 2{sin}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}$

$\beta = {e}^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- cosx}{2sin\dfrac{x}{2} . cos\dfrac{x}{2}}\left[1 - 1 + 2{sin}^{2}\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}$

$\beta = {e}^{\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{- cosx . sin\dfrac{x}{2}}{cos\dfrac{x}{2}}}$

$\beta = {e}^{0}$

$\beta = 1$
$\alpha = \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{{tan}^{3}x - tanx}{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{tanx ( tanx + 1 ) ( tanx - 1 )}{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$\alpha = \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}tanx \times \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\left(tanx + 1\right) \times \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{( tanx - 1 )}{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$\alpha = 1 \times \left(1 + 1\right) \times \lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{( tanx - 1 )}{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= 2\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{tanx - 1}{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= 2\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{sinx - cosx}{cosx . cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$= - 2\sqrt{2}\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}cosx - \dfrac{1}{2}sinx\right)cosx . cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)$

$\alpha = - 2\sqrt{2}\lim_{x \to \pi / 4}\dfrac{cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}{cosx . cos\left(x + \dfrac{π}{4}\right)}$

$\alpha = - 4$

So, the equation whose roots are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is

${x}^{2} + 3x - 4 = 0$

Hence, $a = 1, b = 3$

questions.solution:
Given limit can be written as

$L = \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}}\dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} - \sqrt{2{sin}^{- 1}x}}{1 - x} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2{sin}^{- 1}x}}{\sqrt{\pi} + \sqrt{2{sin}^{- 1}x}}$

Let $K = \lim_{x \to {1}^{-}}\dfrac{{cos}^{- 1}x}{1 - x}$ and put $x = cos\theta$, we get

$K = \lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{θ}{2} . 2}{\sqrt{2} . sin\dfrac{θ}{2}} = \lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{2}{\dfrac{sin\dfrac{θ}{2}}{\theta2}} = \sqrt{2}\left[∵ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{sinx}{x} = 1\right]$

questions.question: Let $f: \mathbf{R} \rightarrow(0, \infty)$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(3)=18, f^{\prime}(3)=0$ and $f^{\prime \prime}(3)=4$. Then $\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left(\frac{f(2+x)}{f(3)}\right)^{\frac{18}{(x-1)^{2}}}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $T = \lim_{x \to 1} \left( \dfrac{f(x+2)}{f(3)} \right)^{\dfrac{18}{(x-1)^2}}$ ; $1^{\infty}$ form
$\Rightarrow T = e^{\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{18}{(x-1)^2} \left( \dfrac{f(x+2) - f(3)}{f(3)} \right)}$
$\Rightarrow T = e^{\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{18}{(x-1)^2} \left( \dfrac{f(x+2) - f(3)}{18} \right)}$
$\Rightarrow T = e^{\lim_{x \to 1} \left( \dfrac{f(x+2) - f(3)}{(x-1)^2} \right)}$ $\dfrac{0}{0}$ form, apply L'pital
$\Rightarrow T = e^{\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{f'(x+2)}{2(x-1)}}$ ; $\dfrac{0}{0}$ form, apply L'pital
$\Rightarrow T = e^{\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{f''(x+2)}{2}}$ $= e^{\dfrac{4}{2}} = e^2$
$\Rightarrow \log_e(T) = 2$

questions.question: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - b{log}_{e}\left(1 + x\right) + cx{e}^{- x}}{{x}^{2}sinx} = 1$, then $16\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}\right)$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given: 

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - b{log}_{e}\left(1 + x\right) + cx{e}^{- x}}{{x}^{2}sinx} = 1$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a{x}^{2}{e}^{x} - b{log}_{e}\left(1 + x\right) + cx{e}^{- x}}{{x}^{2} \cdot x \cdot \dfrac{sinx}{x}} = 1$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a{x}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{1 !} + \dfrac{x2}{2 !} + . . .\right) - b\left(x - \dfrac{x2}{2} + \dfrac{x3}{3} + . . .\right) + cx\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{1 !} + \dfrac{x2}{2 !} + . . .\right)}{{x}^{2} \times x} = 1$

Coefficient of $x = 0$

$⇒ - b + c = 0 . . . \left(iii\right)$

Coefficient of ${x}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ a + \dfrac{b}{2} - c = 0 . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ a - \dfrac{c}{2} = 0$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{c}{2}$

Coefficient of ${x}^{3} = 1$

$⇒ a - \dfrac{b}{3} + \dfrac{c}{2} = 1 . . . \left(iii\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{c}{2} - \dfrac{c}{3} + \dfrac{c}{2} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{2c}{3} = 1$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{3}{2} = b$

$⇒ a = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ 16\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}\right) = 16\left(\dfrac{9}{16} + \dfrac{9}{4} \times 2\right)$

$⇒ 16\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2} + {c}^{2}\right) = 81$

questions.question: If $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x{sin}^{2}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in R$, then which of the following is NOT correct?
questions.solution:
Given,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x{sin}^{2}x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{{x}^{3}\dfrac{{sin}^{2}x}{x2}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha{e}^{x} + \beta{e}^{- x} + \gammasinx}{x3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now using expansion of given function in terms of $x$ we get,

$= \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\alpha\left(1 + x + \dfrac{x2}{2 !} + \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right) + \beta\left(1 - x + \dfrac{x2}{2 !} - \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right) + \gamma\left(x - \dfrac{x3}{3 !} + \ldots\right)}{x3}$

Now for limit to exist constant terms should be zero

$⇒ a + \beta = 0 . . . . \left(1\right)$

Also coefficient of $x$ should be zero

$⇒ \alpha - \beta + \gamma = 0 . . . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Also coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ should be zero

$⇒ \dfrac{α}{2} + \dfrac{β}{2} = 0 . . . . . . . \left(3\right)$

So limit becomes, $\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{{x}^{3}\left(\dfrac{α}{3 !} - \dfrac{β}{3 !} - \dfrac{γ}{3 !}\right) + {x}^{4}\left(\dfrac{α}{3 !} - \dfrac{β}{3 !} - \dfrac{γ}{3 !}\right)}{x3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Now putting the value of limit we get,

$\dfrac{α}{6} - \dfrac{β}{6} - \dfrac{γ}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . . . . . . \left(4\right)$

Now on solving equation $1, 2, 3 \text{ and } 4$ we get,

$⇒ \alpha = 1, \beta = - 1, \gamma = - 2$

Now putting these in all option we get, $\alpha{β}^{2} + \beta{γ}^{2} + \gamma{α}^{2} + 3 = 0$

We have,

$\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\alphax{e}^{x} - \beta{log}_{e} ( 1 + x ) + \gamma{x}^{2}{e}^{- x}}{x{sin}^{2}x}\right] = 10$

Neglecting higher powers.

$\lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{x ( \alpha - \beta ) + {x}^{2}\left(\alpha + \dfrac{β}{2} + \gamma\right) + {x}^{3}\left(\dfrac{α}{2} - \dfrac{β}{3} - \gamma\right)}{x3} = 10$

questions.q: The product of all possible values of $\alpha$, for which $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos(\alpha x)\cos((\alpha+1)x)\cos((\alpha+2)x)}{\sin^2((\alpha+1)x)}\right) = 2$, is:
questions.question: The product of all possible values of $\alpha$, for which $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1 - \cos(\alpha x)\cos((\alpha+1)x)\cos((\alpha+2)x)}{\sin^2((\alpha+1)x)}\right) = 2$, is:
questions.solution:
Using the standard expansions for small $x$, $\cos \theta \approx 1 - \dfrac{\theta^2}{2}$ and $\sin \theta \approx \theta$.

The given limit can be written as:

$\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{\alpha^2 x^2}{2}\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{(\alpha+1)^2 x^2}{2}\right)\left(1 - \dfrac{(\alpha+2)^2 x^2}{2}\right)}{((\alpha+1)x)^2}$

Neglecting higher powers of $x$, the numerator simplifies to:

$1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\left(\alpha^2 + (\alpha+1)^2 + (\alpha+2)^2\right)\right) = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\left(\alpha^2 + (\alpha+1)^2 + (\alpha+2)^2\right)$

Substituting this back into the limit:

$\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{x^2}{2}\left(\alpha^2 + (\alpha+1)^2 + (\alpha+2)^2\right)}{(\alpha+1)^2 x^2} = \dfrac{\alpha^2 + (\alpha+1)^2 + (\alpha+2)^2}{2(\alpha+1)^2}$

We are given that this limit is equal to $2$. Therefore:

questions.question: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{\sin(x^3 - 5x^2 + ax + b)}{(\sqrt{x-1} - 1)\log_e(x-1)} = m$, then $a + b + m$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $x - 2 = t$. As $x \to 2$, $t \to 0$.

The given limit can be written as:

$\lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sin((t+2)^3 - 5(t+2)^2 + a(t+2) + b)}{(\sqrt{t+1} - 1)\log_e(t+1)} = m$

The denominator can be approximated for small $t$ as:

$\lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sqrt{t+1} - 1}{t} \cdot \dfrac{\log_e(t+1)}{t} \cdot t^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 1 \cdot t^2 = \dfrac{t^2}{2}$

For the limit to be finite, the argument of the sine function in the numerator must have $t^2$ as its lowest degree term in its expansion.

Let $P(t) = (t+2)^3 - 5(t+2)^2 + a(t+2) + b$

$P(t) = t^3 + 6t^2 + 12t + 8 - 5(t^2 + 4t + 4) + at + 2a + b$

$P(t) = t^3 + t^2 + (a - 8)t + (2a + b - 12)$

For the limit to exist, the constant and linear terms must be zero:

$a - 8 = 0 \Rightarrow a = 8$

$2a + b - 12 = 0 \Rightarrow 16 + b - 12 = 0 \Rightarrow b = -4$

Substituting $a$ and $b$ back into $P(t)$:

$P(t) = t^3 + t^2$

The limit becomes:

$m = \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sin(t^3 + t^2)}{t^2 / 2}$

$m = \lim_{t \to 0} \dfrac{\sin(t^2(t+1))}{t^2(t+1)} \cdot \dfrac{t^2(t+1)}{t^2 / 2} = 1 \cdot 2 = 2$

Therefore, $a + b + m = 8 - 4 + 2 = 6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.solution:
Given: $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{cos}^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{x\right\}2\right){sin}^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{x\right\}\right)}{\left\{x\right\} - \left\{x\right\}3}$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}f\left(x\right) = \lim_{h \to 0}f\left(0 + h\right)$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}f\left(h\right)$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{cos}^{- 1}\left(1 - {h}^{2}\right){sin}^{- 1}\left(1 - h\right)}{h\left(1 - {h}^{2}\right)}$

$⇒ RHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{cos}^{- 1}\left(1 - {h}^{2}\right)}{h}\left(\dfrac{{sin}^{- 1}1}{1}\right)$

Let ${cos}^{- 1}\left(1 - {h}^{2}\right) = \theta ⇒ cos\theta = 1 - {h}^{2}$

$⇒ RHL = \dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{θ}{1 - cos\theta}$

$⇒ RHL = \dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1 - cos\theta}{\theta2}}$

$⇒ RHL = \dfrac{π}{2}\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ RHL = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ R = \dfrac{π}{2}$

Now finding left hand limit,

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{x \to {0}^{−}}f\left(x\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}f\left(- h\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{{cos}^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{- h\right\}2\right){sin}^{- 1}\left(1 - \left\{- h\right\}\right)}{\left\{- h\right\} - \left\{- h\right\}3}$

$⇒ LHL = \dfrac{π}{2}\lim_{h \to 0}\left(\dfrac{{sin}^{- 1}h}{h}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{- h + 2}\right)$

$⇒ LHL = \dfrac{π}{4}$

questions.question: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function and $f(x)=\lim _{\mathrm{n} \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^{3}} \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}^{2}}{3^{x}}\right]$. Then $12 \sum_{\mathrm{j}=1}^{\infty} f(\mathrm{j})$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
Let [·] denote the greatest integer function. We have $f(x) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n^3} \sum_{k=1}^n [\frac{k^2}{3^x}]$.
For large $n$: $\sum_{k=1}^n [\frac{k^2}{3^x}] \approx \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k^2}{3^x} = \frac{1}{3^x} \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} \approx \frac{n^3}{3 \cdot 3^x}$
Therefore: $f(x) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n^3} \cdot \frac{n^3}{3 \cdot 3^x} = \frac{1}{3^{x+1}}$
Computing the infinite series:
$\sum_{j=1}^\infty f(j) = \sum_{j=1}^\infty \frac{1}{3^{j+1}} = \frac{1}{3^2} + \frac{1}{3^3} + \frac{1}{3^4} + \cdots$
$= \frac{1}{9} \cdot (1 + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{9} + \cdots) = \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{1}{1 - 1/3} = \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = \frac{1}{6}$
Therefore: $12 \sum_{j=1}^\infty f(j) = 12 \cdot \frac{1}{6} = 2$

questions.question: The value of $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{n2},$ where $r$ is non-zero real number and $\left[r\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $r,$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
We know that $r \le \left[r\right] < r + 1$

$2r \le \left[2r\right] < 2r + 1$

$3r \le \left[3r\right] < 3r + 1$

$⋮ ⋮ ⋮$

$nr \le \left[nr\right] < nr + 1$

On adding all the above inequalities, we get

$r + 2r + \ldots + nr \le \left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right] < r + 2r + . . . nr + n$

Using $1 + 2 + 3 + . . . + n = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}, n \in N,$

$\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r \le \left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right] < \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r}{n2} \le \dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{n2} < \dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n}{n2}$

Now, $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{n ( n + 1 ) \cdot r}{2 \cdot {n}^{2}} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{n}^{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) \cdot r}{2 \cdot {n}^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

and $\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2} \cdot r + n}{n2} = \lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{{n}^{2}\left\{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{n}\right) \cdot r + \dfrac{1}{n}\right\}}{2 \cdot {n}^{2}} = \dfrac{r}{2}$

So, by Sandwich Theorem, we can conclude that

$\lim_{n \to \infty}\dfrac{\left[r\right] + \left[2r\right] + . . . + \left[nr\right]}{n2} = \dfrac{r}{2} .$
